title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 3rd District
area: Southwest Louisiana, including Acadiana and Lafayette.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

summary.text: Clay Higgins is the U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District, an Army veteran and former law enforcement officer who is a core member of the House Freedom Caucus. He serves as a senior member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and chairs its Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, and also sits on the House Armed Services Committee.

background.text: Army veteran and law enforcement officer who maintains an active commission and Louisiana State POST certification.
Resides in Lafayette, in the district he represents.

priorities.text: Site describes him as advancing "Constitutionalist principles" and as a champion for smaller government, lower taxes, secure borders and individual freedoms.

positions.summary: Official biography describes him as a champion for secure borders.
Official biography describes him as a champion for lower taxes and smaller government.

record.text: Serves as Chairman of the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, where his office says he investigates government corruption; also serves on the House Armed Services Committee's Subcommittees on Seapower and Projection Forces and on Readiness.
Is a core member of the House Freedom Caucus.

summary.text: Tia LeBrun is a teacher and curriculum leader from Terrebonne Parish and a member of the United Houma Nation, running as a candidate with no party affiliation for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District on a platform of education access, healthcare affordability and insurance reform.

background.text: Born and raised in Terrebonne Parish; a member of the United Houma Nation and, her survey says, three generations of working-class women.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Louisiana State University (2004) and a graduate degree from the University of New Orleans (2012); works as a teacher and curriculum leader.

priorities.text: Says Louisiana families are "being crushed by the highest insurance rates in the nation" and calls for a national plan for insurance affordability and disaster mitigation.
priorities.quote: Louisiana families are also being crushed by the highest insurance rates in the nation. We need a national plan for insurance affordability and disaster mitigation that protects homeowners, drivers, and small businesses—before the next storm hits.

priorities.text: Wants affordable healthcare and childcare for every parent, and is "fighting for paid family leave, healthcare not tied to employment, universal preschool, and two years of free community college."
priorities.quote: Every parent should have access to affordable healthcare, childcare, and education. Families should be able to grow, learn, and live well without going broke. That's why I'm fighting for paid family leave, healthcare not tied to employment, universal preschool, and two years of free community college.

priorities.text: Says she believes in "personal freedom—the right to make decisions about your own body, your family, and your future without government or corporate interference."
priorities.quote: Above all, I believe in personal freedom—the right to make decisions about your own body, your family, and your future without government or corporate interference.

positions.summary: Says she believes in personal freedom, "the right to make decisions about your own body," without government interference.
positions.quote: Above all, I believe in personal freedom—the right to make decisions about your own body, your family, and your future without government or corporate interference.

positions.summary: Calls for healthcare not tied to employment and affordable healthcare for every parent.
Campaigns for paid family leave and universal preschool.
